answer: The request_id is the idempotency key. Any call with a request_id that already produced an order is the same request: return that order, with no second charge and no second reservation.
answer_after_change: The request_id is the idempotency key. A repeat with the same customer and the same items (in any order) returns the original order with no new charge or reservation. If the request_id comes back with a different customer or different items, raise IdempotencyConflict and charge nothing.

topic: Failed requests and retrying with the same id
answer: If the first attempt failed (out of stock or payment failed), nothing was placed, so the app may send the same request_id again and it should be processed as a new attempt.
Only TransientPaymentError is retried, 3 attempts in total including the first. A declined card fails immediately. Keep the existing backoff; tests pass a no-op sleep.
Stock is reserved when the order is placed. If the order is not placed for any reason, every unit reserved for that request goes back. Cancelling a placed order also returns its stock.

Orders come back in creation order. Following next_page_token until it is None returns every matching order exactly once. The last page returns None as the token, and there is no trailing empty page. limit is 1 to 100; anything else is a ValueError, and so is a token that is not one we issued.

Only PLACED orders can be cancelled. Cancelling a SHIPPED order raises InvalidTransition. Cancelling an order that is already cancelled just returns it and must not return stock twice. An unknown id raises OrderNotFound.
Refunds are handled by a separate billing job, out of scope here. Cancelling only changes the status and returns stock.
Assume a single process for this exercise; no locking or database. It is fine to mention what you would change in production (a unique constraint on request_id, key expiry), but do not build it.
All money is integer cents in one currency. The order total is the sum of quantity times unit price.
Keep the public method signatures as they are; other teams call them. Adding private helpers is fine.
